children: Iron ore prices are higher as market sentiment improves, while gains are likely to be capped by ample supply and weakening steel demand in China, Everbright Futures analysts write in a note. Global shipments remain elevated. Persistent demand weakness and easing cost support are likely to keep prices under pressure, with traders watching changes in hot-metal output and port inventories, they add. Upside risks include stronger-than-expected policy stimulus and a sharp decline in port arrivals, they say. The most actively traded January iron ore contract on the Dalian Commodity Exchange is 1.3% higher at CNY664.0 a ton. (jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)
